state.case_summary:
An 83-year-old Hispanic woman visited Bascom Palmer Eye Institute with complaints of vision loss in the left eye, floaters, and flashing lights for one to three months. Her medical history included hypertension, cardiomyopathy, chronic bronchitis, and dementia with psychosis managed with haloperidol. An MRI of the brain conducted one month prior showed no mass lesions. She had a scaly rash on the left side of her face, arm, and leg for over a year, which improved significantly with an antibiotic for a gastrointestinal infection but was still present. The rash had not been biopsied. Ocular examination showed 20/30 vision in the right eye and 20/400 in the left eye. The vitreous fluid in the left eye contained cells, with considerations of an old, decolorized vitreous hemorrhage or an inflammatory reaction. There was no inflammation in the anterior segment. A small white fibrotic macular lesion was barely visible. Vision improved to 20/80, but the vitreous cells increased in the periphery.

The vitreous was sent for flow cytometry and cytology studies. The macular lesion was unchanged; there were no other retinal lesions.

What is the most likely diagnosis?
